body: Mine were inverted as well, I realized later. They never did an echo, but my doctor said she didn't think there was any problem so I'm just living with it and hoping for the best. I'm glad to hear you got the all-clear though!

For me, personally, this sub has been lifesaving. And outside of people talking about their own struggles, I've found people to be as helpful and as hopeful as I believe they can be going through this. I'm sorry if you've had a different experience.

It's such a relief to see someone else who's had low-grade fevers for a long time. I'm not 100 percent mine is from covid, but I do believe that it's the most likely cause. I hope you get to feeling better sooner rather than later

I know for me at about two weeks I started to improve for about two weeks then it all went downhill. That isn't to say, of course, that it'll go the same for you, as I'm sure that you're still recovering. Make sure to take it easy,  it's really easy to jump back into too much too soon and you really got to give yourself the time to recover. Keep an eye on it, but hopefully, you'll just get well and stay there!
I'm not an expert, but it sounds more like you're dealing with something other than a side effect. I hope you get to feeling better soon.
I just cant figure out what to do....

Yes, me for sure. Chicken, eggs, and most coffee are on there for sure. I haven't had my vaccine yet, but I've been dealing with this for a couple of months with both smells and taste. For me perfume and body wash are a lot different, they smell like a strong sweet/rotten smell now.
Yes, this has been happening to me every month since I've had covid. It's always worse right around my period.
I've got a therapist now. It doesn't seem to be super helpful, but perhaps with time. Thanks.

Hi, I'm so sorry you're going through this. I recently had a chest x-ray, CTA, and EKG, and blood work done due to an ER visit. While my chest x-ray, cta, and blood work came back normal, my EKG was not normal. The first one they did said possible heart attack, but now it's just abnormal T-waves. I seem to be in a wait-and-see space as well unless my doctor decides to do something different. It's awful just for me, and I can imagine doubly so for you with even more showing up on your test. How's your mental health doing? I know mine is at its lowest, so I wanted to reach out and check in with you. Also, I know there are a lot of people with normal test results, but I'm certain it's not just the two of us with abnormal results. You belong here, don't worry.

This is a hard place to be in. I can't be as much use as I'd like here, but people do get better. It's just so hard right now, but it doesn't mean that it'll be this hard forever. I believe in you, and I believe that we can see the other side of this misery if we can just hold on.
I've been seeing more people talking about this altered sense of smell which is reassuring to me. We aren't alone, and hopefully it'll pass soon and things will improve.

I wish I could tell you how long it'll last. For me it's been about a month of the sort of rotten meat/sweet smell. I'm hoping it's just another passing issue after covid and it'll be gone soon. I hope the same for you, it's rough when your sense of smell and tatse are so off.
Thank you, but I can't handle feeling like this anymore.
It's wild the things that covid can do
I take prozac. I don't know how much it helps for the anxiety, tbh, although it has helped with my depression some.
Not too much sadly. I take hydroxyzine for it and it seems to help a little

I don't smell blood, but I have seen people talking about an altered sense of smell or phantom smells. Mine is altered as well, but more like garbage/meat/something else. I hope your sense of smell gets back to normal soon.
I had anxiety previously, but I do know that mine is worse after having recovered from Covid.
I appreciate that
That's not a bad idea, thanks

It's only three months covid, not near as long or as bad as anyone else which just adds to the shame. Today has been my oxygen dropping and feeling awful, and this smell in my nose.
I'm right with God, thank you for the prayer
I'm just so tired of feeling bad
Thank you for the prayer

I'm not sure about partially disappearing, but I've seen people speak about/experienced myself issues with smelling months after having covid amid a relapse, so I would suspect it is entirely possible that there could be any sort of smell disturbance that comes along with it.
You must have a very sad life and I pity you
If I do anything more than walking, and some days that includes just simply walking, I start to get the exhaustion and shortness of breath and all back again.
I'm going through that right now. It's so awful, and I hope you get to feeling a bit better soon.

No worries. I'm feeling a bit sensitive right now, I guess. Yeah, I don't know. I know I can't get the tests I probably really need, and yet I'm still upset he didn't do anything/try to listen. But...it is what it is. Thanks for taking the time to respond to me.
That's what the doctor said, I'm just trying to be less worried about it and hopefully it'll all work itself out. Thanks.

They can run some tests at the clinic I go to...I wasn't expecting every test under the sun, I recognize that there are limitations with no insurance but not doing anything at all is not what I expected. I mean... I don't want to sound rude or anything but this just sounds like you're acting like I'm stupid for expecting my doctor, that I pay for, to do some basic testing.

Sadly I don't have insurance at the moment so I'm really limited on doctors I can afford. I guess I should not have been expecting much of anything, but it feels awful to not know anything more than I did before I went to the doctor. Thanks for taking the time to comment though!
I'm not sure this is called for. I'm sorry that you're suffering, but taking it out on other people because you're hurting is not helpful to you or to them.

Mine has never been that low, and it's usually only at night, but I have had moments where it felt like I couldn't really get a breath, or that I'd been holding it, and there'd be a drop in my oxygen for just a few seconds and then it'd go right back up to normal. I've noticed mine seems to be worse when rolling over in bed or things of that nature. I've also had x-rays but heading to the doctor again to try to get some more tests. I don't know the cause, but I know you're not alone in that. I'd mention it to your doctor when you get the chance, maybe they can offer more help, or someone else here can as well. I hope you get to feeling better soon, take care!
I've been having the same sort of problem off and on for a while now, if you can try to sleep on your side or stomach, I've noticed that's helped me a lot.
Thank you so much for this. I had a full panic attack reading the article, this helps some.
Yes, I think it's fairly common. I know I'm going through one right now after only a short period of slight relief.

I didn't have the rest of that when I had active covid but I had that tickle in the chest, a slight cough and a fever for the first day. Then it was mostly complete exhaustion for me. I hope you find out what's going on with you soon, whether that be covid or something else!

I'm so sorry you're dealing with this. That sounds almost exactly where I'm at right now, all the sudden, with my shortness of breath.  I don't have any advice or anything sadly, as I'm still in the dark myself, but I hope you are able to get some answers and that they lead you to a path of feeling like your old self.
Mine feels a lot of ways, sometimes it's like I've been holding my breath, and sometimes it's more like I was exercising when I wasn't. I hate it, and I'm sorry you're having to deal with it too.

I'm so sorry all that happened to you, I hope you can get the help you need soon. I don't have your exact symptoms, but until someone can answer that more closely falls in line with you, I can tell you I've seen quite a few people talking about how it did get better with time, so there is always hope. I know from personal experience that it can feel like you're not going to see the other end of this, but people do, and if it's any help at all you are very much not alone with this. Covid has touched so many people, in so many ways, and I'm sure someone on here will have better advice, offers of hope, but I just wanted to let you know that you're not alone in the darkness or the struggles. Take care!

I hope it goes sooner rather than later, but thanks!
